title: Implement Error unconditionally via core::error::Error, retiring std features
description:
## What the MSRV bump unlocked

core::error::Error stabilized in Rust 1.81. The workspace MSRV is now 1.88, so a no_std crate can implement Error unconditionally -- no std feature, no cfg.

Four crates currently gate a std feature, and for most of them that feature exists to turn on an Error impl:

- pkix-dane -- std does ONLY this. Its Cargo.toml says so outright: "enables the std::error::Error impl on DaneError. Nothing in this crate needs std otherwise." The feature can be deleted entirely.
- pkix-path -- nine std::error::Error references.
- pkix-revocation -- two.
- pkix-aia -- two, BUT its std feature has a second job and cannot simply be deleted: it also unlocks the AiaError::IoFailure variant, whose kind: std::io::ErrorKind field is std-only. core has no ErrorKind equivalent. So pkix-aia keeps a std feature for IoFailure while the Error impl becomes unconditional.

## Why it is worth doing

A no_std consumer of pkix-dane or pkix-path today gets an error type that does not implement Error, so it cannot participate in a source() chain or be boxed as dyn Error, purely because of a Rust-version constraint that no longer applies. Deleting the feature in pkix-dane's case also removes a feature combination from the test matrix.

Note the knock-on: pkix-chain currently depends on pkix-dane with features = ["std"] specifically so Error::Dane can expose source(). That turns into a plain dependency.

## Related, same theme

core::net stabilized in 1.77, so IpAddr / Ipv4Addr / Ipv6Addr are available without std. pkix-identity uses std::net (IP-literal SAN matching) and declares no std feature, so it may be std-only today for that reason alone. Worth checking whether it could be no_std on core::net -- it would line that crate up with the rest of the core crates. Verify before assuming; the crate may be std for other reasons.

## Acceptance

[ ] pkix-dane's std feature deleted; DaneError implements Error unconditionally
[ ] pkix-path and pkix-revocation implement Error unconditionally; their std features either deleted or documented as still earning their place
[ ] pkix-aia's Error impl is unconditional while std continues to gate IoFailure, with the comment updated to say that is now its only job
[ ] pkix-chain drops the features = ["std"] on its pkix-dane dependency
[ ] Whether pkix-identity can become no_std on core::net is checked and the answer recorded
[ ] no_std builds still clean; feature matrix updated
